description: Documented expectations for the Test Case Generator demo processes. Every condition below is asserted by tests/integration/test_test_case_sample_data.py.

processes.name: p2p_standard_po
processes.title: Procure to Pay - standard purchase order
processes.summary: The financially sensitive, heavily integrated process. Its description mentions invoices, goods receipts and payments, it names four integrations and four roles, so every configured priority escalation signal fires.

processes.name: pm_notification
processes.title: Plant maintenance - raise a maintenance notification
processes.summary: The negative control. One role, no integration, no financial vocabulary, so no escalation rule fires and every test case keeps its test type's base priority.

processes.name: migration_vendor
processes.title: Vendor master migration - cutover load
processes.summary: A cutover load, deliberately requested with more test types than test cases so the uncovered-type path is exercised: the generator drops the lightest types and says so instead of silently ignoring them.

processes.name: fiori_approval
processes.title: Fiori purchase requisition approval
processes.summary: An approval app with six roles and no financial posting. Only the access-related test types escalate, which is what the role-count rule is for.

scenarios.condition: All three priority escalation signals fire
scenarios.expectation: The process description contains configured escalation keywords, four integrations are named (>= the threshold of 3) and four roles are named (>= the threshold of 4).
scenarios.assert: keyword_hits is not empty, integration_count >= 3, role_count >= 4

scenarios.condition: System integration tests are escalated above their base priority
scenarios.expectation: SIT has a base priority of high and the keyword rule applies to it, so every SIT case in this suite is critical.
scenarios.assert: every sit test case has priority 'critical'

scenarios.condition: Nothing escalates for a quiet process
scenarios.expectation: No escalation keyword appears, no integration is named and one role is named, so every case keeps its test type's configured base priority.
scenarios.assert: keyword_hits is empty and every test case priority equals the configured base priority of its type

scenarios.condition: More test types requested than test cases
scenarios.expectation: Six types are requested and four cases are asked for, so the two types listed last receive no case, are reported as uncovered and produce a note. The headline type of the process - data migration, listed first - is kept.
scenarios.assert: uncovered_test_types == ['security', 'regression'], note_count >= 1, and a data_migration case exists

scenarios.condition: Only the access test types escalate on role count
scenarios.expectation: Six roles are named, so authorization and security escalate one level; the process description contains no financial keyword, so UAT does not.
scenarios.assert: authorization and security cases are above their base priority while uat cases are at theirs

scenarios.condition: Every planned case is complete without any AI
scenarios.expectation: With drafting switched off, every case is built from the configured templates and still has at least the configured minimum number of steps.
scenarios.assert: every test case has source 'template' and step_count >= min_steps

scenarios.expectation: Each identifier follows the configured template and carries its test type's id_code, numbered from 1 within the type.
scenarios.assert: test_case_id values are unique per suite and match the type's id_code
